summary: Russia launched a massive combined attack on Odesa with drones, missiles, and bombs, targeting port infrastructure. Ukrainian forces reported casualties and damage in multiple regions. Russian advances near Illinovka and Privilege were noted.
key_points: Russia conducted a 3-hour combined attack on Odesa using up to 70 Shahed-131 drones, Geran-3/4 missiles, and Su-34-launched Kh-59/Kh-69/Kh-31P rockets, targeting port infrastructure (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70935).
Russian strikes on Ukrainian ports caused over 2% GDP damage, reducing monthly grain exports from 6M to 4M tons, with wheat prices hitting a two-year high (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32626).
Russian forces liberated Zelenoye in Zaporozhye, clearing 200+ buildings, while fighting continued in Sumy, Kharkov, and Kursk regions (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32639).
Ukrainian strikes on Kherson's critical infrastructure and Russian attacks on Belgorod civilians (3 injured) were reported (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32626; @tass_agency/391420).
Russian forces advanced near Illinovka and Privilege, diverting Ukrainian resources (Source: @DeepStateUA/23760).
Ukrainian defense minister highlighted severe damage to 300+ gas stations and energy infrastructure from Russian attacks (Source: @UkraineNow/83585).
Ukrainian MP Nina Yuzhanina warned of worsening budget shortfalls due to war costs (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32651).

sections.threat_assessment: Russia's sustained attacks on Ukrainian port infrastructure and energy facilities threaten economic stability and civilian safety. The use of Geran-3/4 missiles and Shahed-131 drones indicates a focus on precision strikes, while Ukrainian budget shortfalls risk undermining defense capabilities. Russian advances near Illinovka and Privilege suggest a strategic push to consolidate occupied territories.
sections.regional_response: Ukrainian forces continue retaliatory strikes on Russian-occupied territories, including Kherson and Zaporozhye. Civilian casualties in Belgorod and Sumy highlight the human cost of cross-border attacks. Ukrainian officials emphasize the need for international support to address infrastructure and budget crises.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian use of Geran-3/4 missiles and Shahed-131 drones in Odesa attacks suggests a shift toward precision strikes on critical infrastructure. Ukrainian budget shortfalls and reliance on outdated ground robots for medical evacuations indicate resource constraints. Russian advances near Illinovka and Privilege may signal a broader offensive strategy to secure eastern territories.
